Ram 1500 SRT Gets Into the Slammed Widebody Street Mood, Though Only Across Fantasy Land
7 photos
Photo: trapndeth / Instagram
Ram Trucks is having a period of grace – they subdued Jeep and stole its crown as Stellantis’ best-selling brand in America not long ago and also launched a series of great pickup trucks, all based on one simple thing, which is the return of the Hemi V8 under the hood of the Ram 1500 models.
Just recently, the 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee also got a Foose Edition just in time for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, and rode low on the red carpet with 1,000 hp laid to the ground. In Europe, Ram is launching the Rampage, at long last, as their mid-size-like option for a fashionable lifestyle, with two versions, each with its dedicated powertrain.
Let’s also not forget about the return of the mighty 2027 Ram 1500 TRX SRT, which recently encountered a Ford F-150 Raptor R and proved which one is the faster truck. Fans certainly appreciate the credentials, shared with the Rumble Bee SRT model – the 6.2-liter supercharged Hemi V8 used in the previous iteration now makes no less than 777 hp and 680 lb-ft of torque or 922 Nm, backing the 720-hp Ford F-150 Raptor R into a corner and reclaiming the crown of high-performance ICE adventure trucks.
The Ram 1500 SRT TRX celebrated the relaunch of the Street and Racing Technology (SRT) division when it was unveiled on January 1, 2026, and since then has quietly amassed its ‘super’ power for the off-road adventures that lie ahead. But what if someone wants it on the street and only on the street?
Many would say that you just need to catch a 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee SRT instead. However, that’s still not enough for some folks – especially a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI. More precisely, TRAPNDETH, the virtual artist who wants to "trap death to stay alive" (aka " trapndeth " on social media), has created a slammed widebody truck for the ages – an SRT with the Ram looks and the allure of a Fast & Furious build.
Instead of sporting off-road credentials like the Ram 1500 TRX SRT or mild street allure like the Rumble Bee, it goes full throttle with the CGI and slams itself into the ground so hard that it becomes flatter and wider at the same time. As such, it now has a complete widebody aerodynamic kit featuring a new front with a massive lip spoiler, a muscular hood, sculpted fender flares, a new rear with an integrated bed cover and ducktail spoiler, as well as a massive diffuser.
Around the sides are new side ‘steps’ and also massive-lipped alloy wheels, signaling that this build is ready for cool things both on the street and at the track. You won’t be doing much hauling or off-roading with it, since the stance is taking it as close as possible to the ground – so much so that even an ant would fear for its life when seeing that massive front spoiler. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by TRAPNDETH (@trapndeth)

1973 Pontiac LeMans Found in Neighbor's Garage, Minor Restoration Now Needed
41 photos
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics
You won’t find many of these LeMans Sport Coupes these days. That’s right, this is a 1973 LeMans Sport Coupe, and according to the current owner, it spent years locked in a garage.
The car is being described as “very unmolested,” though the paint appears to be the first obvious thing that’s been changed. The car wears a cosmetic GT treatment, but the owner is honest and says that it looks like it was repainted some years ago.
No further specifics are available at this point, but it’s still a Pontiac, and it’s still a LeMans Sport Coupe. I doubt it’ll remain available for too long, as long as the price is correct.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics Pontiac ’s big engines were struggling to remain relevant in the early ‘70s. The new regulations and the rising insurance costs pushed more and more buyers to smaller engines. The GTO suffered, and so did other models whose main point was the performance under the hood.
The LeMans continued to be a popular name in the United States, and despite General Motors still keeping some potent engines around, it was also looking beyond the muscle under the hood.
The new Luxury LeMans, whose purpose was to impress with exquisite features, was the living proof. It got a center armrest covered in Morrokdie vinyl or Bravo cloth and Morrokide, front bucket seats in Morrokide, a custom cushion steering wheel with simulated walnut inserts, wood details on the glove box door, and so many other goodies.
The LeMans Sport Coupe was supposed to retain Pontiac’s appetite for a boost of adrenaline behind the wheel without necessarily going for massive engines. “You expect sporty-looking cars from Pontiac. And we have an exciting new one for you,” Pontiac said.
That’s exactly what the LeMans Sport Coupe was all about, as it was supposed to look sporty without being sporty.
While buyers could also get the GTO package , the engine lineup started with a lazy 250 six whose purpose was to provide buyers with an efficient ride. The 350 - the most popular engine this year - could be had with two or four barrels, and so could the 400. A 455 four-barrel was offered alongside a 455 SD on the two-door LeMans and the Sport Coupe.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics This LeMans Sport Coupe is fitted with a 350ci engine paired with an automatic transmission. “It runs and drives very good,” according to the owner, but that’s all the information we’re getting at this point.
There’s one thing that intrigued me, so I recommend that buyers who are pondering making an offer contact the seller and arrange an in-person inspection. The owner says this car is mostly unmolested, so the 350 V8 engine under the hood should also be untouched. That’s not something you see every day, especially considering that the car has been sitting for several years in a garage and that it has never been rebuilt.
The seller claims some receipts dating back to the ‘80s are also available, so you should check these in person to figure out if this V8 unit has previously received any substantial work.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics Otherwise, this Pontiac looks good, and I don’t think that the rust damage is a major concern. I would still raise it on a lift to check the underside, but the seller claims that the only rust spots are on the lower body. They should be easy to deal with, though it’s probably a good idea to get closer to this car and check both the paint and these signs of rust more thoroughly.
I don’t see any bubbling behind the paint, but these are just photos posted online. The seller claims they also have videos revealing the car more thoroughly, so ask for them if you’re interested in a purchase.
The cabin also looks to be in good shape, but some repairs would still be needed, including on the seats. The driver’s seat shows its age, but dealing with the damage we see in the pics isn’t a major challenge for someone with the right experience.
The owner says the vehicle has recently been serviced, so it now has a new exhaust and tires. It sells with 3 sets of keys and a complete air conditioning system that’s already installed on the car but doesn’t work due to what seems to be a broken blower.
Photo: eBay seller lousclassics As I said earlier, these cars are definitely worth a chance, especially if they are priced correctly.
The owner of this LeMans Sport Coupe believes $9,900 is just a fair expectation, but they also enabled the Make Offer option on eBay to let people submit their offers easily. 91 people have added this car to their watchlists, so there’s a chance it’ll leave for a new garage before the listing expires in 22 days.
The car is parked in New York Mills, New York, and considering its shape, you may not need to spend additional dollars on shipping because you should be able to drive it to your shop on its wheels.
Via // eBay

This Camper Van Is a Warm Mobile Abode Built for Year-Round Comfort Wherever the Road Leads
22 photos
Photo: Vantra
In the case of some camper vans, it's not an exaggeration to call them homes on wheels – they can be as comfortable as a simple studio apartment, but a lot more practical. Take the rig I'd like to share with you today as an example.
What we have here is a project based on a 2026 Ford Transit with a 148" wheelbase, a high roof, and an AWD drivetrain. It was professionally built by Vantra, a Wilmington, North Carolina-based company that specializes in custom Ram ProMaster and Ford Transit AWD camper vans.
As always, let's begin the tour with the exterior. First off, the van rides on black Method wheels wrapped in Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires.
At the rear, you'll come across a spare tire carrier / ladder combo. Use it to climb on top of the van, and you'll discover a powder-coated aluminum roof rack holding a Fiamma manual awning and two 200 W solar panels.
Like a lot of premium mobile homes, this van sports a set of flares. Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed inside in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's flares are paint matched to the van's body and come with windows with sliding screens.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vantra Stepping inside, a warm and well-crafted interior will greet you. Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for grey woven vinyl flooring, a slatted cedar ceiling, and cabinetry with bamboo faces. The look is complemented by white Corian solid surface countertops and some black accents, like the kitchen hardware or the cabinet and drawer handles.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you've set up camp. This simple seating setup is completed by a Lagun table.
The first part of the living space is the kitchen positioned dead ahead of the entrance. It features a deep black stainless steel sink, a 115-liter Dometic fridge with a tiny freezer compartment, and a portable induction stove. Moreover, a vent fan above will help draw out the smells and fumes from cooking.
Two overhead cabinets, a small drawer, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. The latter hides a 4-gallon (15-liter) electric water heater and a single-stage water filtration system.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Vantra Next, we have a bench with a Lagun table on the opposite side, by the entrance. If you lift the bench's hinged top, you'll reveal some storage space. There's more than meets the eye here – this compartment has a false bottom that hides a heater underneath.
Despite the limited interior real estate, Vantra found the space to install a Van Wife Components shower stall. It's made from powder-coated aluminum and measures 24 x 24 inches (61 x 61 centimeters). It houses a shower with a removable sprayer and a portable toilet.
Just like in most camper vans, the rear part of the living space is reserved for sleeping. The bedroom offers a 6-inch-thick, queen-size memory foam mattress and two upper cabinets.
Your bulkiest items will most likely fit in the van's garage, which is underneath the bedroom. It's accessible directly from the living space or through the back of the van, after opening the rear doors.
Photo: Vantra
Besides offering a bunch of room for storage in its middle part, the garage has two tall boxes on the sides that hold the bed platform and accommodate part of the utility systems.
Power is on the right side – the rig's electrical heart is a 10 kWh Bluetti RV5 system. It can be charged via three sources: shore power, solar power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running thanks to an alternator charger. If you use these correctly and efficiently, you might never run out of juice while on the road.
On plumbing, the van is equipped with a 24-gallon (94-liter) freshwater tank, a 22-gallon (83-liter) greywater tank, a 4-gallon (15-liter) water heater, and an outdoor shower connection.
This van was built for year-round comfort, regardless of where you travel. Two systems make the rig four-season-capable: a 48V Velit A/C unit and a gas-powered Velit 12V heater. Moreover, the builders added 3M Thinsulate insulation and sound deadening throughout the van.
Photo: Vantra The "command center" for the utility systems is conveniently located above the entrance. It includes a large touchscreen display that lets you monitor and control the power and water systems, a thermostat, and dimmer switches for four lighting zones.
All in all, this fully-equipped Transit camper van by Vantra is not only designed to keep going long after the pavement ends, but it also keeps you nice and comfortable regardless of where and when you travel.

2028 Ford Mustang Cobra For S650 Generation Springs Out From Behind the CGI Curtain Looking Feisty
16 photos
Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
The Ford Motor Company traversed a rather tough spot with the S650 iteration of the iconic Ford Mustang , as it didn’t live up to the sales expectations imposed by the S550 predecessor until now. Alas, in terms of potential, it’s massively ahead.
For starters, you can’t have anything like the Ford Mustang with a V8 straight from the dealership – the General Motors pony car, Chevrolet Camaro, has been retired since late 2023, and Stellantis has also killed off the Challenger, leaving only the Charger to fend for itself. But the latter, based on the new STLA Large architecture, is a bit of a shadow – it comes with EV and inline-six twin-turbo options.
The 2027 Ford Mustang, meanwhile, can be had with an affordable EcoBoost inline-four turbo solution and 315 hp or as the GT with the iconic 5.0-liter Coyote V8. Actually, there’s another naturally-aspirated V8 model – the Dark Horse, which has 500 hp – and a couple of supercharged V8s.
Those are the flagship Mustang GTD, which is basically a GT3 racer for the street, and the new Dark Horse SC coupe and convertible, which also uses the 5.2-liter supercharged Predator V8 under the hood and many racing-proven features to give fans a taste of what has become known as the successor to the iconic Shelby GT500.
Now that’s all fine and dandy, but it seems that Ford isn’t done yet – just recently the rumor mill proudly announced that it caught whispers of the Blue Oval preparing yet another version of the S650 Mustang, or even two. More precisely, it seems that the automaker is prepared to bring back the beloved Cobra and Cobra R nameplates, with both used as intermediate versions tucked between the Dark Horse and Dark Horse R, where there’s plenty of hp space – from 500 to 795 hp is a long way to go, indeed.
If the rumors are correct, then the revived Ford Mustang Cobra and Cobra R will become the spiritual successors to the S550 Shelby GT350 and GT350R. Naturally, that has attracted a lot of attention, including from across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI, where the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators have started preparing their latest unofficial, hypothetical design projects based on these rumors – and have come up with brand-new S650 Cobra Rs.
But that’s not all, because Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a new Cobra – this time around the ‘base’ model instead of the more extreme Cobra R version like his fellow pixel master.
Anyway, the CGI expert has used the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC as the starting point but reworked the design and the iconic alloy wheels to better fit the Cobra persona. Cool, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Jim (@jlord8)

BMW M3 Gets Its Pixels Rearranged To Become a Fat Low-Rider
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign
Most news involving the BMW M3 these days are all about its successor, the Neue Klasse model expect to launch in 2028, or its mechanically-unrelated zero-emission alternative that’s understood to come out next year.
This one does not follow the traditional recipe, though. In fact, there isn’t anything remotely traditional about it, as it’s had its pixels rearranged, and the result is a quirky-looking sedan with extra muscles and some very sharp corners that sits extremely close to the ground.
In fact, it has such a low ground clearance that even a pebble could ruin its new splitter that was attached to a different bumper. The latter has redesigned air intake, and retains the double-coffin grille, albeit with a different pattern. Further back, we can see that this BMW M3 has a new hood that looks extremely aggressive, as well as fender flares, and new side skirts.
There is also a roof-mounted scoop for show and tell reasons, as it is not functional. Additional highlights include the massive wing bolted to the trunk lid, a quite discreet spoiler, a new rear bumper, and a large diffuser that looks like it came from a different era. The roof appears to have been made of carbon fiber, the wheels are new, and seem to have positive camber at the rear, and the suspension has been significantly altered.
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign This low-riding BMW M3 Sedan features a light blue paint finish on the outside, sports the BMW anniversary logos, and has plenty of black details. It also features tinted windows that do not allow us to catch a glimpse of the interior, and there is a very good reason for that.
As you have likely figured out, the sports sedan in question is not real. It is the work of @onb.artdesign, which describes it as being “a track monster in the middle of autumn,” adding that “Every line of carbon fiber is like a pact made with the asphalt.” Those are some very big words for what is in essence a quirky-looking machine, and for one, I am glad that this thing is not real.
Before wrapping it up, we will remind you that the current BMW M3 packs a straight-six engine with twin turbos. The mill has a 3.0-liter displacement, and pumps out 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW) in the most basic variant of the car, which takes 4.1 seconds from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). The Competition has 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW) on tap, and the Competition xDrive brings 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) to the output party, as well as a rear-biased all-wheel drive system.
The mid-range variant sprints to 60 mph in 3.8 seconds, and the AWD one does it in 3.4 seconds. Pricing starts at $83,500 (MSRP) for the former and $88,600 for the latter, and the base M3 kicks off at $79,300 in the States. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Onur Bakır (@onb.artdesign)

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Help Me Pick My Next Car – Spoiler Alert: It’s Not Going To Be Easy!
13 photos
Photo: BMW
If there’s one thing that brings us all together, it is the car virus , this incurable disease that has eaten through our finances ever since we got our first paycheck. Some of us have lost contact with those who we once thought we’d have by our side forever due to our car obsession, and some have simply managed to move on.
What does the latter part mean? Well, in my case, a nice car that relatively reliable, looks good, drives good, and does not tend to bankrupt me in case things go south. On top of that, my ride is comfortable and quiet, because I have reached an age when straight-piping feels like absolute nonsense, and stiff suspensions are definitely a no-no. By the way, been there and done that, as I absolutely loved cars with the suspension travel of a dining table a couple of decades ago.
From a gearhead’s perspective, because this is what this story is all about, I am absolutely disappointed in everything the car industry stands for today. Have you driven modern vehicles? You probably have, and while you can still get a nice and very reliable truck/ SUV /pickup, I am not into high-riders and never were, even if I used to own a crossover from Jeep at one point that I absolutely hated. You can read that story here , by the way, though preferably after you are done with this one.
I don’t have a numerous family, so station wagons are out of the question, though to be honest, I wouldn’t mind a nice C8 Audi RS 6 Avant. I could probably get one with a stretch, but then again, that wouldn’t be a financially-wise decision. Coupe and convertibles are not exactly my thing either, unless we are talking about a luxury-oriented fixed-roof model. You know, something like a C217 Mercedes S-Class Coupe.
Photo: BMW Then again, buying one of those would again not be a wise decision, as not only they’re not the most reliable out there, but they are also quite plasticky. And I absolutely hate car crickets. Therefore, sedans are definitely my cup of tea. And while I’m at it, these would need to check numerous boxes in order to be appealing to me. Comfort it a must, good looks, too, and pretty much everything I already mentioned a few paragraphs above.
If you’ve been following my stories, then you know that I am fond of two car manufacturers: BMW and Lamborghini. And while the latter is out of reach, for now anyway, not to mention that their rides are not exactly great daily drivers, nor to they go easy on the wallet. And no, Lambos do not mean the Urus. That’s a rebodied Volkswagen Touareg with numerous other mods, and while I can understand the fact that it’s a huge moneymaker for the Raging Bull, I would never buy one , regardless of how much money I have in the bank.
Thus, it’s pretty much all about BMWs for me. And they have to be sedans for the above reasons. The 2 Series Coupe is a great driver’s car, and the M2 is absolutely dreamy. But I don’t plan on spending too much money on gasoline, especially since the juice has significantly gone up nowadays. The 3er is an absolute icon, and the M3 is an even bigger one. But I want something bigger and a lot more comfortable.
The 7 Series seems pointless to me, as it’s simply too big and heavy, and therefore, I settled for the 5 Series. In fact, I’m currently at the third 5er, and all of them have been F10s by choice. I didn’t get to enjoy my first due to a reason called divorce. The second one was very Spartan, though it did go extremely easy on my wallet during some challenging times for me, and when those times ended, I sold it and bought my third F10.
Photo: BMW It needed to check to major (for me) boxes: feature an automatic transmission, and most of my driving is urban, and I live in a very crowded city, and have a sunroof, because I love to look at the sky above every now and then. And it ended up coming with much more equipment. Leather upholstery, power-adjustable seats, a Bang & Olufsen (not Harman Kardon, by the way) premium sound system, ambient lighting, a head-up display, xDrive AWD, adjustable suspension, and so on.
I’m now in my third year of owning this F10 BMW 5 Series LCI , and while it is still a great machine in my opinion, I am now starting to search for my next one on the used car market. I’d like a newer one, but the G60 is not my cup of tea. I find it ugly both inside and out, and the facelifted iteration that’s in the making as we speak will enter the Neue Klasse era, so it would feel more like a downgrade rather than an upgrade.
The G30 does not look that good compared to the F10, at least on the outside, so what should I get? I Don’t like the new Audi A6, the modern-day Mercedes E-Class is too much of a screen fest. Jaguar is now on the white stuff, I don’t fancy Lexus’ and Infiniti’s rides. In my eyes, Volvo is a Europe-based Chinese marque at this point (ahem, Geely), and don’t even get me started on EVs. You could say the Porsche Panamera, but it’s not exactly a looker, is it? On top of that, the maintenance would be challenging to say the least.
Unless I am missing something (Cadillac, erm, nope!), that pretty much sums up this class. I don’t want a mainstream car from Mazda, Toyota, and so on, even if there is no major difference anymore between these things and premium ones, especially if you aim for a top grade. So, what am I left with? Probably my current Bimmer , which would be a lot nicer with a nicer set of wheels and a new timing chain. So, I’d better keep writing, as the latter is a must next year.

Finally, a Rolls-Royce Ghost That Doesn’t Cost an Arm and a Leg!
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc
While some say the Rolls-Royce Ghost is the best full-size luxury sedan out there, others would opt for a Mercedes-Maybach S-Class or a Bentley Flying Spur, arguing that these are better.
And we think that you believe in the former model. After all, here you are, looking to find out more details about the car pictured above, including the model year, mileage, and how much it costs, among other things, because this one is for sale in the United States of America, and won’t affect your finances badly enough that the missus won’t talk to you anymore.
To the average Joe, this Rolls-Royce Ghost looks modern, but real petrolheads know that they are looking at the previous generation . This model was assembled from 2009 to 2020, and it is based on the same platform as the F10 BMW 5 Series, the F01 7 Series, and its two-door grand touring siblings, namely the Wraith and the Dawn.
This model measured up to 219.3 inches (5,569 mm) from bumper to bumper in the EWB (extended wheelbase) configuration, and was 212.6 inches (5,399 mm) long in the regular variant. The space between the axles measured 136.4 inches (3,465 mm) in the former, and 129.7 inches (3,295 mm) in the latter.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc A V12 engine (what else?) breathes air from behind that imposing grille, and it is a 6.6-liter mill in this case, paired with an eight-speed automatic transmission, and rear-wheel drive. The twin-turbocharged V12 was rated at 562 hp (419 kW/570 ps) and 575 pound-feet (780 Nm) of torque when the car rolled off the line, enabling 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) in less than five seconds, and a top speed electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph).
This pictured Rolls-Royce Ghost is a 2015 model year car. It features a blue look on the outside, and it is unknown whether it’s a paint finish or a wrap, as the vendor hasn’t mentioned it. There are no chrome details anymore, as everything was blacked out. The wheels are also black, and so its the interior, with its high-end leather upholstery, wood trim, traditional buttons and knobs, and an overall design that hasn’t aged badly at all.
We found this previous-generation British luxury sedan on Instagram, where it was advertised by @imad_mcc. The vendor said that the odometer read 28,836 miles (46,407 km) at the time of cataloging, so you are looking at a low-mileage machine.
